events.content:
Fixed. Navigation to the product page was slow because the page awaited `getInventory()` directly in the page component, and that function calls `await connection()`, which forces the entire page to render at request time. With `cacheComponents` enabled, that left no static shell — the router had to wait for the server round-trip before showing anything, including the static title.

I restructured `app/product/page.tsx` to move the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component wrapped in a `<Suspense>` boundary. Now the title "Premium Widget" is part of the prerendered static shell and appears immediately on navigation, while the stock count and price stream in (showing "Loading inventory…" briefly).

The build confirms it: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content" — instead of fully dynamic. (The build also auto-updated `tsconfig.json` with Next's mandatory settings; that's standard Next.js behavior, not something I changed by hand.)

content.text:
Fixed. Navigation to the product page was slow because the page awaited `getInventory()` directly in the page component, and that function calls `await connection()`, which forces the entire page to render at request time. With `cacheComponents` enabled, that left no static shell — the router had to wait for the server round-trip before showing anything, including the static title.

I restructured `app/product/page.tsx` to move the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component wrapped in a `<Suspense>` boundary. Now the title "Premium Widget" is part of the prerendered static shell and appears immediately on navigation, while the stock count and price stream in (showing "Loading inventory…" briefly).

The build confirms it: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — "prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content" — instead of fully dynamic. (The build also auto-updated `tsconfig.json` with Next's mandatory settings; that's standard Next.js behavior, not something I changed by hand.)
